about.title: About Wordleland
about.body1: Wordleland is a shared scoreboard for a group of friends who play Wordle every day. Results come in from the group chat and land here as a leaderboard, form over time, and a grid view of who played what.
about.body2: Built as a small side project, not a product. The source is open if you want to see how it works or run your own.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Wordleland is self-hosted for one private group. This says what it keeps about the people who use it, and why.
privacy.stored.heading: What is stored
privacy.stored.body: Your email address, for signing in and password resets. A Signal account identifier and your last-seen display name, if your results arrive from the group's Signal chat. Your Wordle results. If an admin corrects an entry, a record of what it said before. A question the group's bot could not answer, as text only and without who asked it, for 30 days.
privacy.why.heading: Why
privacy.why.body: To run the shared login, to match a Signal message to the right person, and to keep a trail of any correction an admin makes.
privacy.who.heading: Who can see it
privacy.who.body: Your own account details are visible only to you. Admins can see the group's roster and results to run the board. A read-only share link, if one exists for this installation, shows scores only — no email addresses or Signal identifiers.
privacy.cookies.heading: Cookies
privacy.cookies.body: Signing in, and remembering a theme or language choice, uses a few cookies. None of them are used for tracking, advertising, or shared with anyone outside this installation.
privacy.removal.heading: Leaving the group
privacy.removal.body: Leaving disables an account rather than deleting it, so past corrections keep their trail. Ask whoever runs this installation if you want your data handled differently.

reply.help: I can answer who leads or is last (this month, a past month, this or last week, the last N days, all time), the standings, whether somebody can still win and what happens if somebody gets a certain score, streaks, form and who is steadiest, today's puzzle or any day's results, the hardest puzzle and weekday, how many 2s somebody has, who wins the most days, two players head to head, a player's profile and months, the records, the group, who posts first, and what a word means. Mention me and ask.

reply.failed: I couldn't work that one out. Try asking it another way.
reply.failed.2: That one got away from me. Could you put it another way?

reply.rules.which: I can explain: miss, average and points, streak, month, hard mode, form, ranked, what I know.
reply.rules.miss: A miss is a day you didn't post. It counts as 7 in the month and over the last N days, not on the all-time board.
reply.rules.average: Your average guesses per game, lower is better; an X counts as 7. Points are hundredths: 12 points is 0.12.
reply.rules.streak: Solved days in a row. An X or a day not played breaks it; today doesn't until it's played.
reply.rules.month: Everyone's average over the month's days, a missed day as 7, lowest wins. Ties share the place; the result posts when the last day closes.
reply.rules.hardmode: The asterisk on a share. It never changes the score; it only breaks a tie on the day.
reply.rules.form: Your average over the last 30 puzzles (needs 10 games), against your overall average.
reply.rules.ranked: Ranked needs 10 games and one in the last 30 puzzles. Everyone else is listed below, with the reason.
reply.rules.data: I only see the scores people post — guesses, X's, hard mode, when it was posted. Never the words, and not anyone's starting word.
